sentences.text: Researchers analyzed data from a population-based cohort survey conducted in Norway between 2017 and 2019, including 2039 adults with complete data.
Participants who had previously suffered a stroke, heart attack, or heart failure were excluded, and their headache types were determined using established questionnaires.

While initial comparisons showed smaller cardiac volumes in people with migraine and tension-type headache, only tension-type headache remained linked to a significantly lower left ventricle volume after accounting for other factors.
Additionally, the speed of blood flow into the heart during relaxation was significantly lower in people with migraine with aura, though there was no sign of heart failure.

The authors suggest a possible link between tension-type headache and subtle changes in the size of the heart's left chamber, noting that more research is required to verify these findings and understand their medical importance.
